text:
inc-bot: INCIDENT ALERT · customer gateway streaming errors · severity: P1 · affected tenant: MeridianBank · symptom: persistent websocket disconnects + exponential retry storms causing backend worker saturation

ryan (oncall): paging ryan -> I'm awake, looking

andrew (customer-eng): seeing a spike of 502/timeout on our app gateway for MeridianBank since ~22:05 UTC. Customers report chat UIs dropping mid-stream, clients retrying and multiplying connections.

elaine (sre): grabbing logs now. Can you confirm this is via the enterprise VPC gateway (private deployment) and using dedicated pool-alpha?

andrew (customer-eng): yes VPC GW in us-west-2, dedicated pool-alpha, websocket sticky session. We pushed a new client yesterday but the server side shows repeated CONNECT -> CLOSE loops.

sam (platform): quick check: gateway metrics show a 3x increase in open sockets and a spike in upstream 504/connection_timeout between 22:04–22:12. Backend workers are at 95% CPU, queuing backlog growing.

elaine (sre): probable symptom: client retry policy without jitter + short client backoff -> thundering herd. Also backend processing for stream init path taking longer (DB hot partition).

ryan (oncall): immediate mitigations we can do: 1) throttle connection rate for MeridianBank at the GW (rate-limit new WS handshakes) 2) bump gateway idle/read timeout to 35s (was 15s) to reduce reconnect churn 3) turn on token-based connection gate (drop rapid reconnects) 4) route a slice of traffic to a warm standby pool (dedicated pool-beta) for graceful capacity absorb. Can we do those asap?

sam (platform): I'll apply handshake rate-limit and short-circuit health routing to pool-beta. Pushing config now:
```
# temporary nginx-like gateway snippet
map $http_upgrade $is_ws { default 1; }
server {
  listen 443;
  location /ws/ {
    limit_conn_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=meridian_conn:10m;
    limit_conn meridian_conn 8;  # throttle new handshakes
    proxy_send_timeout 35s;
    proxy_read_timeout 35s;
    proxy_pass http://upstream_pool;
  }
}
```

sam (platform): applied limit_conn (meridian_conn=8) and proxy timeouts increased. Also bumped connection gating rule to drop clients with >6 reconnects in 1m.

olivia (solutions): pinged MeridianBank SREs: asked them to add jitter to retry logic and to temporarily disable aggressive reconnect. They acknowledged and will deploy a client fix in the next 10m.

andrew (customer-eng): MeridianBank confirmed they pushed a client-side backoff patch to staging, rolling to prod in 5–8m.

elaine (sre): I'm seeing successful handshakes to pool-beta; new connection rate down ~60% after rate-limit. Worker backlog slowly draining. Still seeing occasional 502s from upstream app (long tail).

ryan (oncall): intermediate mitigation: enable graceful polling fallback for clients that can't sustain WS (we have polling endpoint). Olivia coordinate with them on toggling fallback for heavy sessions.

olivia (solutions): told them how to flip fallback header X-Use-Polling: true. They will enable for ~5% of sessions from problematic IP ranges as a canary.

sam (platform): note: increased timeouts and rate-limits will raise token cost slightly; tracking. Also I added a temporary anomaly rule in the console: if upstream latency > 1.5s for init path, autoscale pool-alpha by +2 replicas.

elaine (sre): diagnostic logs snippet showing client pattern:
```
[22:06:12] meridian-conn-id=abc123 event=ws_open
[22:06:13] meridian-conn-id=abc123 event=ws_close reason=read_timeout
[22:06:13] meridian-client-ip=10.4.7.82 retry_count=1
[22:06:13] meridian-conn-id=def456 event=ws_open
[22:06:13] meridian-conn-id=def456 event=ws_close reason=read_timeout retry_count=2
```
Looks like many clients open then immediate close -> retry.

ryan (oncall): can we surface the specific IPs causing the storm and block/blackhole them for 60s as a surgical mitigation?

sam (platform): running quick query: rg "retry_count>" /var/log/gateway/meridian* | awk '{print $5}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head -n 10 -> top offenders: 10.4.7.82, 10.4.7.90, 10.4.7.103. I pushed firewall rules to drop new handshakes from those CIDR /32 for 60s.

andrew (customer-eng): updated MeridianBank that we blackholed a few offending client IPs and asked them to identify if those are bots. They said yes, two of them are a misconfigured mobile client fleet.

elaine (sre): checking DB. There was a hot partition from a billing-ledger scan that slowed init path by ~800ms. Mitigated by reindex job cancel and promoted a read replica for the stream-init queries. Latency on init path down to ~220ms.

ryan (oncall): good. Status check: connection failures dropped from 18%->4% in last 6m, total open sockets trending down. Meridian reported far fewer client drop tickets.

olivia (solutions): MeridianBank confirms user reports dropped by 90% and their detection shows less retry traffic. They will roll permanent client backoff fix tomorrow.

elaine (sre): follow-ups: 1) add jitter guidance and sample code to Meridian onboarding docs 2) persist a per-tenant circuit-breaker in the gateway for future storms 3) add a test in our chaos harness to simulate retry storms against dedicated pools 4) post-incident RCA later.

ryan (oncall): I'm going to close the P1 alert in 30m if metrics remain stable. Handoff: elaine will own postmortem and follow-ups, sam will track platform config change PR for persistent circuit-breaker, olivia will coordinate customer client fix.

inc-bot: ACTIONS LOGGED · P1 created 2290012345 · oncall=ryan · status=mitigated (rate-limits + timeout bump + blackhole) · followups_assigned=[elaine, sam, olivia]

elaine (sre): updating channel with timeline and Mitigation steps for the RCA. I'll include metric graphs and the query we used to identify offenders.

sam (platform): adding the temporary nginx snippet and firewall commands to the incident runbook entry.

ryan (oncall): thanks everyone. Stand by for the postmortem. :thumbsup:
